u1: Ladies and gentlemen, the court of history is now in session.
u2: Today's case: a tomb in Siberia, a thousand cannabis seeds, and one very big claim.
u3: Siberia! A huge burial mound called Tunnug 1, in Tyva, in the south of Siberia!
u4: And inside the central chamber, researchers report somewhere between a thousand and fifteen hundred cannabis seeds and fragments!
u5: Source: study published in Science, November 2026.
u6: Radiocarbon dating of six of those seeds places them in the early eighth century BCE.
u7: That is somewhere around twenty-seven or twenty-eight hundred years ago.
u8: The oldest dated evidence of cannabis used to get high!
u10: Hold on. "Used to get high" is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
u11: The seeds are not the key evidence. The hair is.
u12: Researchers report finding traces of THC, and a related compound called CBN, in strands of human hair from the central chamber.
u14: Or proof the hair spent two thousand years next to a pile of cannabis.
u16: One outside researcher said the data does not distinguish consumption from external exposure.
u17: Hair buried beside the seeds could simply have picked up residue.
u18: Another outside expert called the CBN levels "hard to believe" for wild cannabis.
u19: Contested. Both views are in the sources.
u20: Why does this matter? Because the ancient Greek writer Herodotus described Scythian people using hemp seeds.
u21: He placed it after a funeral, as a way to cleanse themselves.
u22: He also wrote that they crawled under felt covers, threw hemp seeds on red-hot stones, and howled with joy in the vapour!
u23: Herodotus wrote that centuries after this tomb. And historians debate how much of it he saw himself.
u24: Archaeologists place Tunnug 1 in the oldest Scythian horizon.
u25: But the tomb does not establish whether cannabis was consumed during the burial ceremony itself.
u26: Seeds: found, and radiocarbon dated. Hair chemistry: contested. Use in burial ceremonies: not established.
u27: The court finds: the seeds are real. The dates are solid. The high is unproven.
u31: Next time: a Roman fort in Wales, and a legend that may or may not be true.
